text: What is the Nasdaq 100? Index of 100 large non-financial firms. The Nasdaq 100 is a benchmark index tracking 100 large non-financial companies traded on the Nasdaq stock exchange. It is tech-heavy, and investors use it to gauge how the biggest US technology shares are performing as a group.. A tech stock rout that began on Wall Street on Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026, spread through Asian markets on Friday, Nov. 6, after the US midterm elections raised fears about AI regulation.. The index is abbreviated NDX, NDQ, NAS100 or US100. It is weighted by market capitalization, with the largest single company capped at a maximum weight of 24 percent. Because of that weighting, a few very large firms can move the whole index. On Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026, the tech-focused Nasdaq fell 5.5 percent, according to Al Jazeera and BBC reporting; BBC put the loss at about $2.5 trillion in market value. The Nasdaq 100 dropped 6.3 percent that day. The selloff followed the US midterm elections on Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026, in which Democrats won both the Senate and the House. Investors feared tighter regulation of AI and of the data centers that power it. The sell-off spread to Japan, South Korea and Taiwan on Friday, Nov. 6, where the Nikkei fell 6 percent.

What does bear market territory mean? Nikkei case, Nov. 6, 2026. Bear market territory means a stock index has fallen about 20 percent or more from its recent high, a level that signals a broad downturn in share prices. On Nov. 6, 2026, Japan's Nikkei 225 index entered bear-market territory during a global tech stock selloff.. A tech stock rout that began on Wall Street on Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026, spread to Asian and European markets on Friday, with Japan's Nikkei and South Korea's Kospi falling sharply after the US midterm elections raised fears about AI regulation.. Japan's Nikkei 225 fell as much as 6 percent on Friday, Nov. 6, 2026, and in doing so entered bear-market territory, according to the index's movement that day. Its worst week since 2020 accompanied the drop, and Taiwan's TAIEX index fell 9 percent at one point during the same session. The selloff began on Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026, after the US midterm elections. The Nasdaq 100 dropped 6.3 percent that day, and the S&P 500 fell 4.4 percent, its worst day in 18 months. Analysts linked the decline to worries that a Democratic Congress would tighten scrutiny of AI infrastructure and data centres, which could raise costs and delay projects. For the historical comparison, the United States entered a bear market on Oct. 9, 2007, and it lasted until March 9, 2009, during which the S&P 500 lost roughly half its value.

What is the Kospi? South Korea's main stock index, Nov. 6, 2026. The Kospi is South Korea's main stock market index, a single number that tracks the share prices of all common stocks traded on the Korea Exchange. Traders watch it as the country's broadest gauge of stock prices, much as Americans watch the S&P 500.. A tech stock rout that began on Wall Street on Thursday, Nov. 5, 2026, spread to Asia on Friday, Nov. 6, and the Kospi was among the hardest-hit indexes, with trading halted temporarily. Markets remained under pressure in Asian trading.. The index is formally called the Korea Composite Stock Price Index. It covers every common stock listed on the Stock Market Division of the Korea Exchange, which was previously known as the Korea Stock Exchange. On Friday, Nov. 6, 2026, the Kospi fell more than 8 percent shortly after the opening bell. Trading on the Kospi was temporarily halted across the market, and the index later ended the day down 6 percent, according to BBC reporting. The initial drop was reported by Al Jazeera and NBC News. The fall followed a sharp drop in US tech shares on Thursday, Nov. 5, when the Nasdaq fell 5.5 percent. The selloff was tied to fears that Democrats, who won control of both houses of Congress in the Nov. 3 midterm elections, would bring tighter rules on artificial intelligence and data centres. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, both South Korean AI chipmakers, were among the heaviest losers. Analysts say the Kospi moves closely with the global AI spending cycle.
